paras: I'm applying for the Software Engineering Internship because your posting describes the work I enjoy most: taking an internal tool that people depend on and making it fast and dependable. The line about owning a service end to end, from schema to on-call, is the part that stood out.

This summer at Example Logistics I built a shipment-search service with FastAPI and PostgreSQL that replaced a shared spreadsheet for the operations team. The hard part was the nightly import: it took 40 minutes and sometimes overlapped with the morning shift. Batching the writes and adding one index brought it to 6 minutes, and the test suite I added to CI caught two regressions before they shipped.

In the Data Systems Lab I benchmark retrieval systems, which taught me to distrust a result until I can explain it. When our evaluation numbers looked too good, I traced them to a leak between the training and test splits and fixed it, even though the corrected numbers were less exciting.
I'd bring the same habits to your team: measure first, write the test, and keep the people who use the tool in the loop. Thank you for considering my application.
